metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >15% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often fails to adjust; add 5–10% downward bias for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is positive and model forecast is below recent 10-day moving average, model underestimates; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply mean reversion: if forecast > 1.5x recent 30-day avg, cap at 1.5x; if < 0.8x, adjust up by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., 3+ positive, 3+ negative), model tends to lag; add 2–5 day lag correction to forecast (i.e., shift down 1–2 days for next 5–10 days).
